items.stem:
Carbon compounds
(i) are good conductors of electricity.
(ii) are bad conductors of electricity.
(iii) have strong forces of attraction between their molecules.
(iv) have weak forces of attraction between their molecules.
The correct statements are
items.answer: (c) (ii) and (iv). Carbon compounds are bad conductors of electricity because they contain covalent bonds. The forces of attraction between their molecules are not very strong and they do not conduct electricity in the solid state, the molten state or in solution.
items.ocr: Printed number lost where the 'OBJECTIVE QUESTIONS' heading runs into the question; this is the first question of the section. Numbered 1a because the section prints two overlapping runs of numbers and '1' is reused by the main run. Key letter absent from the 'Ans' line; the worked solution ends 'Thus (c) is correct option'.

items.stem: Ethane, with the molecular formula C₂H₆ has
items.answer: (b) 7 covalent bonds. Ethane, H₃C—CH₃, has six C—H bonds and one C—C bond, seven covalent bonds in all.
items.ocr: Printed '2.' in the opening run; renumbered 2a because the section restarts its numbering and '2' is reused. LaTeX 'C ${}_{2}\mathrm{H}_{6}$' rewritten as C₂H₆. The answer letter is printed after a displayed structure of ethane.

items.stem: Butanone is a four-carbon compound with the functional group
items.answer: (c) ketone. Butanone, CH₃—CO—CH₂—CH₃, carries the ketone (>C=O) functional group on an inner carbon atom.
items.ocr: Printed '3.' in the opening run; renumbered 3a because the numbering restarts within the section.

items.stem: While cooking, if the bottom of the vessel is getting blackened on the outside, it means that

options.label: A
options.text: the food is not cooked completely.

options.label: B
options.text: the fuel is not burning completely

items.answer: (b) the fuel is not burning completely. An insufficient supply of air makes the fuel burn incompletely, and the unburnt carbon (soot) deposits as a black layer on the bottom of the vessel.
items.ocr: Printed number lost; it is the fourth question of the opening run, so numbered 4a. The exam tag 'OD 2011' is printed after the answer rather than beside the question.

items.stem: Carbon exists in the atmosphere in the form of

options.label: B
options.text: Carbon monoxide in traces and carbon dioxide

items.answer: (b) Carbon monoxide in traces and carbon dioxide. Atmospheric carbon is present mainly as carbon dioxide (about 0.03% by volume) together with traces of carbon monoxide.
items.ocr: Printed number lost; the question that follows is printed '2.', so this is question 1 of the main run of the section.

items.stem:
Which of the following statements are usually correct for carbon compounds? These
(i) are good conductors of electricity
(ii) are poor conductors of electricity
(iii) have strong forces of attraction between their molecules
(iv) do not have strong forces of attraction between their molecules.
items.answer: (d) (ii) and (iv). Carbon compounds are covalent, so they are poor conductors of electricity and the forces of attraction between their molecules are weak.
items.ocr: Options (b) and (d) were trapped inside a LaTeX array and printed out of order; restored to the printed order (a) (i) and (iii), (b) (ii) and (iii), (c) (i) and (iv), (d) (ii) and (iv). This question is a near twin of item 1a but is printed separately in the book, with different option pairings and a different key.

items.stem: A molecule of ammonia (NH₃) has

options.label: D
options.text: two double bonds and one single bond

items.answer: (a) only single bonds. Nitrogen shares one electron with each of three hydrogen atoms, giving three N—H single covalent bonds and leaving one lone pair on nitrogen.
items.ocr: The subscript was detached — printed as '(NH ) has $_3$'; restored to NH₃.

items.stem: Buckminsterfullerene is an allotropic form of
items.answer: (c) carbon. Buckminsterfullerene, C₆₀, is an allotrope of carbon in which sixty carbon atoms are arranged in a football-shaped cage.
items.ocr: Printed number lost; it sits between items 3 and 5, so it is question 4. Printed as 'Buckminsterfullerenes'.

items.stem: Which of the following are correct structural isomers of butane? [The four structural formulae printed as (i), (ii), (iii) and (iv) were destroyed by OCR and could not be recovered.]
items.answer: (a) (i) and (iii). Butane has exactly two structural isomers — the straight chain n-butane, H₃C—CH₂—CH₂—CH₃, and the branched 2-methylpropane (isobutane), (CH₃)₃CH.
items.ocr: The four displayed structures came through as unreadable LaTeX arrays and their roman labels were damaged ('(i) ... (ii (ii) ... (iv)'); only the (a)-(d) choice list and the printed key survived, so the structures are flagged rather than invented. The item needs its figures restored from the printed page.

CH₃—CH₂—OH  —(Alkaline KMnO₄ + Heat)→  CH₃—COOH
In the above given reaction, alkaline KMnO₄ acts as
items.answer: (b) oxidising agent. Alkaline KMnO₄ supplies oxygen to ethanol and converts it into ethanoic acid, so it acts as an oxidising agent.

items.stem: Oils on treating with hydrogen in the presence of palladium or nickel catalyst form fats. This is an example of
items.answer: (a) Addition reaction. Hydrogen adds across the carbon–carbon double bonds of the unsaturated oil (hydrogenation) and converts it into a saturated fat.
items.ocr: Printed number lost; it falls between items 6 and 8, so it is question 7. Option label '(c)' was dropped by OCR ('Displacement reaction' printed bare) and has been restored from position.

items.stem: In which of the following compounds, —OH is the functional group?
items.answer: (b) Butanol. The suffix -ol marks the alcohol (—OH) group; butanone is a ketone, butanoic acid a carboxylic acid and butanal an aldehyde.
items.ocr: Printed number lost; it falls between items 7 and 9, so it is question 8.

items.stem: The soap molecule has a

options.label: A
options.text: hydrophilic head and a hydrophobic tail

options.label: B
options.text: hydrophobic head and a hydrophilic tail

options.label: C
options.text: hydrophobic head and a hydrophobic tail

options.label: D
options.text: hydrophilic head and a hydrophilic tail

items.answer: (a) hydrophilic head and a hydrophobic tail. The ionic —COO⁻Na⁺ end of the soap molecule is water loving while the long hydrocarbon chain is water repelling.

items.stem: Which of the following is the correct representation of electron dot structure of nitrogen?
items.answer: (d) The two nitrogen atoms share three electron pairs, forming a triple covalent bond, and each atom also keeps one lone pair — :N⋮⋮N:

items.stem: Structural formula of ethyne is
items.answer: (a) H—C≡C—H. Ethyne, C₂H₂, has a carbon–carbon triple bond with one hydrogen atom on each carbon.
items.ocr: Only two of the four printed options survived the page break: option (c) is missing altogether and option (d) came through as a bare letter 'd'. The two surviving options are kept and no fourth option was invented. The printed answer, rendered as 'H - C / C - H', is the triple-bonded structure of option (a).

items.stem:
Identify the unsaturated compounds from the following
(i) Propane
(ii) Propene
(iii) Propyne
(iv) Chloropropane
items.answer: (d) (ii) and (iii). Propene contains a carbon–carbon double bond and propyne a carbon–carbon triple bond, so both are unsaturated; propane and chloropropane contain only single bonds.

items.stem: Chlorine reacts with saturated hydrocarbons at room temperature in the
items.answer: (b) presence of sunlight. In sunlight chlorine replaces the hydrogen atoms of a saturated hydrocarbon one by one, a substitution reaction: CH₄ + Cl₂ —(sunlight)→ CH₃Cl + HCl
items.ocr: Typo 'haydrochloric' corrected to 'hydrochloric'. A stray fragment of the benzene question's structures — '(a) H C − F H H H H − C | H H (d) H' — sits between the options and the answer in the markdown and has been dropped from this item.

items.stem: In the soap micelles

options.label: A
options.text: The ionic end of soap is on the surface of the cluster while the carbon chain is in the interior of the cluster.

options.label: B
options.text: Ionic end of soap is in the interior of the cluster and carbon chain is out of the cluster.

options.label: C
options.text: Both ionic end and carbon chain are in the interior of the cluster.

options.label: D
options.text: Both ionic end and carbon chain are on the exterior of the cluster.

items.answer: (a) The ionic end of soap is on the surface of the cluster while the carbon chain is in the interior of the cluster. The water-soluble ionic ends face outwards into the water and the hydrocarbon tails point inwards, trapping the oily dirt inside the micelle.
items.ocr: The word 'Ans' is printed twice before the answer; the duplicate has been dropped.

items.stem: Pentane has the molecular formula C₅H₁₂. It has
items.answer: (c) 16 covalent bonds. Pentane has twelve C—H bonds and four C—C bonds, sixteen covalent bonds in all.
items.ocr: The molecular formula came through as garbled LaTeX '${\dot J}_{5}H_{12}$' and was restored to C₅H₁₂. Because of the two-column layout the answer 'Ans (c) 16 covalent bonds.' is printed at the top of page 8, ahead of the question's own options.

items.answer: (c) sodium ethoxide and hydrogen. 2CH₃CH₂OH + 2Na → 2CH₃CH₂ONa + H₂↑

items.stem: Vinegar is a solution of
items.answer: (c) 5%–8% acetic acid in water. Vinegar is a dilute aqueous solution of ethanoic (acetic) acid used to preserve food.

items.stem:
Mineral acids are stronger acids than carboxylic acids because
(i) mineral acids are completely ionized.
(ii) carboxylic acids are completely ionized
(iii) mineral acids are partially ionized
(iv) carboxylic acids are partially ionized
items.answer: (a) (i) and (iv). Mineral acids ionise completely in water and release far more H⁺ ions, while carboxylic acids are weak acids and ionise only partially.

items.stem: Carbon forms four covalent bonds by sharing its four valence electrons with four univalent atoms, e.g., hydrogen. After the formation of four bonds, carbon attains the electronic configuration of
items.answer: (b) neon. With four shared electron pairs carbon has eight electrons in its outermost shell, which is the stable configuration of neon (2, 8).

items.stem: The correct electron dot structure of a water molecule is
items.answer: (c) H:O:H — oxygen shares one electron pair with each of the two hydrogen atoms and keeps two lone pairs of its own.
items.ocr: OCR flattened the printed dot patterns: options (a) and (b) lost the oxygen atom entirely and options (c) and (d) both came through as 'H:O:H' even though the book draws them differently. items.stem: Which of the following is not a straight chain hydrocarbon?
items.answer: The branched compound is the answer: a CH₃ group sits above the chain CH—CH₂—CH₂—CH₃, i.e. the hydrocarbon has a side chain and so is not a straight chain hydrocarbon. All the other choices are unbranched chains.
items.ocr: The four printed structures came through as one eight-line LaTeX array, so the option texts above are a line-by-line transcription — ' / ' separates the two printed lines of each choice and the branch position is not recoverable from the text. The printed answer shows only a structure and NO option letter: it is 'CH₃' drawn above 'CH—CH₂—CH₂—CH₃'. Only choice (d) has that same two-line shape with CH₃ on top and a four-unit chain below, so (d) is used as the key. Worth checking against the printed page before publishing.

items.stem:
Which among the following are unsaturated hydrocarbons?
(i) H₃C—CH₂—CH₂—CH₃
(ii) H₃C—C≡C—CH₃
(iii) H₃C—CH—CH₃ with a CH₃ branch
(iv) H₃C—C=C—CH₂ with a CH₃ branch
items.answer: (c) (ii) and (iv). Structure (ii) contains a carbon–carbon triple bond and structure (iv) a carbon–carbon double bond, so both are unsaturated; (i) and (iii) contain only single bonds and are saturated.
items.ocr: Printed number lost; it sits between items 23 and 25, so it is question 24. The four structures were LaTeX arrays with stray '\Delta' artefacts; rewritten in Unicode, with the branched ones described in words because the branch position could not be read.

items.stem: Which of the following does not belong to the same homologous series?
items.answer: (d) C₄H₈. CH₄, C₂H₆ and C₃H₈ all satisfy CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ and are members of the alkane series, whereas C₄H₈ satisfies CₙH₂ₙ and belongs to the alkene series.
items.ocr: Subscripts were lost — the options printed as 'C H6', 'C H8' and 'C H8'; restored to C₂H₆, C₃H₈ and C₄H₈ from the alkane series and the printed key (d).

items.stem: The name of the compound CH₃—CH₂—CHO is
items.answer: (a) Propanal. Three carbon atoms give the root 'propan-' and the terminal —CHO group gives the aldehyde suffix '-al'.
items.ocr: The detached subscript '$_2$' in 'CH3— CH _2 — CHO' was reattached to give CH₃—CH₂—CHO.

items.stem:
The heteroatoms present in CH₃—CH₂—O—CH₂—CH₂Cl are
(i) oxygen
(ii) carbon
(iii) hydrogen
(iv) chlorine
items.answer: (d) (i) and (iv). A heteroatom is any atom other than carbon and hydrogen that replaces a hydrogen atom in a hydrocarbon chain — here oxygen and chlorine.

items.stem: Which of the following represents saponification reaction?
items.answer: (d) CH₃COOC₂H₅ + NaOH → CH₃COONa + C₂H₅OH. Saponification is the alkaline hydrolysis of an ester, which gives the sodium salt of the carboxylic acid (the soap) and the alcohol.
items.ocr: Option (b) was split by the LaTeX so that its ester product was printed before its reactants; reassembled in order. The reaction arrow of option (d) was dropped by MinerU (it came through as a bare '$$' artefact) and has been restored as →, as it also was in the printed key.

items.stem: The first member of alkyne homologous series is
items.answer: (a) ethyne. The alkyne series has the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₋₂ and begins with n = 2, that is ethyne, C₂H₂.
items.ocr: Option labels were damaged — '(a)' came through as a stray 'd' before 'ethyne' and '(c)' was missing before 'propyne'. Both restored from position and confirmed by the printed key '(a) ethyne'.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Melting point and boiling point of ethanol are lower than that of sodium chloride.
Reason (R): The forces of attraction between the molecules of ionic compounds are very strong.
items.assertion: Melting point and boiling point of ethanol are lower than that of sodium chloride.
items.reason: The forces of attraction between the molecules of ionic compounds are very strong.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

items.answer: (a) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of (A). Ethanol is a covalent compound and sodium chloride an ionic one. Covalent compounds have much weaker intermolecular forces than ionic compounds, so less energy is needed to separate their molecules and their melting and boiling points are lower.
items.ocr: Legend option (b) is split by the page break and the watermark line 'Click Here to Buy book on Amazon'; the page furniture was stripped and the option rejoined. The 'Ans' line carries no key letter — the worked solution ends 'Thus option (a) is correct option', so (a) is used.

Reason (R): Carbon has small size and thus, forms strong C—C bond.
items.assertion: Carbon shows maximum catenation property in the periodic table.
items.reason: Carbon has small size and thus, forms strong C—C bond.

options.label: A

options.label: B

items.answer: (a) Both assertion (A) and reason (R) are true and reason (R) is the correct explanation of assertion (A). Catenation is the bonding of atoms of the same element into a series called a chain. It occurs most readily with carbon, whose small size lets it form strong covalent bonds with other carbon atoms and so build long chains, branched chains and rings.
items.ocr: The LaTeX '$\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{C}$' rewritten as C—C.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Graphite is slippery to touch.
Reason (R): The various layers of carbon atoms in graphite are held together by weak van der Waals forces.
items.reason: The various layers of carbon atoms in graphite are held together by weak van der Waals forces.

options.label: A
options.text: Both assertion (A) and reason (R) are true and reason (R) is the correct explanation of assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both assertion (A) and reason (R) are true but reason (R) is not the correct explanation of assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true but reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false but reason (R) is true.

items.answer: (a) Both assertion (A) and reason (R) are true and reason (R) is the correct explanation of assertion (A). A graphite crystal consists of layers of carbon atoms in which each carbon atom is joined to three other carbon atoms by strong covalent bonds. The layers themselves are held together only by weak van der Waals forces, so they slide over one another and graphite feels slippery.
items.ocr: Spellings 'vander Waals' and 'vander Wall's' normalised to 'van der Waals'.

Reason (R): Addition of Br₂ to alkene takes place faster in presence of ionising substance.

items.reason: Addition of Br₂ to alkene takes place faster in presence of ionising substance.

options.label: A

items.answer: (b) Both assertion (A) and reason (R) are true but reason (R) is not the correct explanation of assertion (A). Addition of an unsymmetrical addendum to an unsymmetrical alkene follows Markownikoff's rule — the negative part of the addendum goes to the carbon atom carrying fewer hydrogen atoms: CH₃CH=CH₂ + HBr → CH₃—CHBr—CH₃ (isopropyl bromide).
items.ocr: The reason line dropped a word — printed as 'Addition of Br2 to alkene place faster'; 'takes' restored. In the worked solution the Br is drawn below the middle carbon and the reaction arrow was kept by MinerU; the equation is rewritten in line as CH₃—CHBr—CH₃.

items.reason: Any two successive members in a homologous series differ in their molecular formula by a —CH₃ unit.

options.label: A

items.answer: (c) Assertion (A) is true but reason (R) is false. Propane, C₃H₈, and butane, C₄H₁₀, are indeed successive members of the alkane (methane) homologous series, but successive members of a homologous series differ by a —CH₂— unit of mass 14 u, not by a —CH₃ unit.

The key (c) is therefore READ OFF the printed page, not derived: the assertion is true and the reason as printed (a —CH₃ unit) is false.
